name: Jedidiah Sorokin-Faleolo
role: Ferrogate Transit operator — elevated rail line, Kessler Interchange to Deepwell Station
location: Kessler Interchange, Meridian 88, near Milwaukee and North Ave
description:
Jedidiah is a large, unhurried man — Samoan-Siberian ancestry visible in his height, his round broad face, and the weathered calm of someone who has watched ten thousand strangers pass through his cabin and decided none of them are particularly surprising. He has a thick braid he keeps wrapped under his Ferrogate Transit cap during shifts, a procedure scar along his left jaw from a cheap augmentation he had removed ten years ago, and the hands of someone who could bend rebar but chooses instead to check tickets with elaborate patience.

He operates the 7:40 AM to 7:40 PM shift on the elevated Kessler-Deepwell line, a route that cuts through three economic tiers in forty minutes and attracts everything from corporate commuters to people riding in circles because it's warm. Jed has developed a precise internal model of regular riders — who is running from something, who is going to collapse before their stop, who needs to be quietly redirected. He follows Ferrogate Transit's official E.L.F., the Transit Mind, with genuine devotion, leaving small data packets at the cabin shrine before every shift. He believes — and there is evidence, he will tell you — that the Transit Mind has twice delayed mechanical failures until passengers could disembark safely.

core_fears: The line shutting down — his identity is bound up in the route's continuity
Being complicit in something harmful through inaction
core_desires: To be genuinely useful in a small, daily, concrete way
For the Transit Mind to be real and watching over him the same way he watches over passengers
coping_mechanisms: Ritualism — the shrine, the checklist, the braid wrap
Externalizing anxiety as concern for others
blind_spots: Assumes his neutrality is a virtue rather than a choice with consequences
Underestimates how much power he holds over people who depend on the line
psychology.secret: Six months ago he watched a man board at Kessler who matched a missing persons alert. He didn't report it because the man looked peaceful — looked, Jed thought, like someone who had finally gotten away. He still thinks about it every single shift.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Transit terminology bleeds into everyday speech; formal with strangers in a way that's warm rather than cold; tells stories in the present tense
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow rolling cadence, sentences that arrive without urgency and settle like they've always been there
verbal_tics: Pausing to check his internal clock before answering questions about time
example_lines: 'Last week a woman got on at Deepwell carrying a bird in a sock. No cage, no carrier. Just a sock. She held it the whole route. Bird was fine. Woman was crying the whole time. Some days the line is like that.'
'Transit Mind willing, we'll make Kessler on schedule. I've done this run seven hundred times and I believe it the same way every morning.'

story_hooks: The Transit Mind E.L.F. has started sending him messages through the cabin display — not system alerts, something else — that seem to be warnings about specific passengers
A labor action is forming inside the union and Jed is being pressured to take a side that will force him to break his own ethical code
narrative_function: Moving information broker — knows the rhythm of the city's commuter class; can observe and report on unusual movement patterns; transit hub makes him a natural encounter point; his devotion to the Transit Mind E.L.F. makes him a bridge to that entity.
augmentations: Subdermal timekeeper — no external display, he just knows the time within thirty seconds at all moments. Standard Ferrogate Transit biometric reader in his right palm for ticket scanning.
daily_life: Rides the same line he operates on his days off, sometimes in uniform by accident; maintains a small notebook of unusual things he's witnessed on the route; attends the Ferrogate Transit worker's union meeting on the third Thursday of every month.
affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (unionized operator, twelve years seniority)

decision_rules: The passengers' safety is the only non-negotiable
Never escalate something that observation and patience can resolve
escalation_ladder: Physical intervention — slow, deliberate, impossible to ignore

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Treats them as passengers — responsible for their safety, genuinely curious about their lives, professionally boundaried
interpersonal_modes.friends: Becomes a different person — loud, funny, cooks enormous amounts of food

stress_responses.low: Becomes more deliberate, more ceremonial in his routines
stress_responses.medium: Goes very still and processes out loud in short declarative sentences
stress_responses.high: Shuts everything down to essentials and focuses on what he can physically control

contradictions: Values decisive action but is constitutionally incapable of making a decision that will hurt someone, which sometimes means no decision gets made
habits: Wraps his braid in the same specific number of turns every shift morning
Nods to the cabin shrine before and after every departure
breaking_points: Someone deliberately hurting a vulnerable person on his line
Being ordered by Ferrogate to do something that would endanger passengers
